catalog_quote: 2.2. Patrón acentual El acento en esta variante es predecible: 1) En toda palabra flexionada, el acento siempre va a caer en el radical. 2) En las palabras compuestas por 2 o 3 radicales, el acento siempre cae en la sílaba del último radical. Ningún afijo lleva acento. [p.47, §2.1 Patrón silábico:] El zapoteco de SPG es una lengua de raíces predominantemente monosilábicas; las palabras de dos o más sílabas que existen se deben a la afijación de los morfemas gramaticales, los cuales se unen a un radical ya sea como prefijo o como sufijo para expresar su contenido, o bien, por la unión de dos o más radicales que se juntan para formar palabras compuestas.

new_statements.quote: 2.2. Patrón acentual. El acento en esta variante es predecible: 1) En toda palabra flexionada, el acento siempre va a caer en el radical. 2) En las palabras compuestas por 2 o 3 radicales, el acento siempre cae en la sílaba del último radical. Ningún afijo lleva acento.
new_statements.translation: 2.2. Stress pattern. Stress in this variety is predictable: 1) In every inflected word, stress always falls on the root. 2) In words compounded from 2 or 3 roots, stress always falls on the syllable of the last root. No affix bears stress.

I re-rendered scan page 33 from the PDF we hold myself (page render, 80 dpi) and it shows book pp.48-49; the right half is identical to the held lc_pages/. Book p.49, section 2.2 'Patrón acentual' reads exactly: 'El acento en esta variante es predecible: 1) En toda palabra flexionada, el acento siempre va a caer en el radical. 2) En las palabras compuestas por 2 o 3 radicales, el acento siempre cae en la sílaba del último radical. Ningún afijo lleva acento.' -- verbatim as quoted (the first reader's quote prepends the section heading '2.2. Patrón acentual.', which is also on the page). Surrounding context read: p.47 section 2.0-2.1…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable and morphologically determined: it falls on the (predominantly monosyllabic) root; prefixes (TAM etc.) and suffixes/enclitics are never stressed; in compounds of two or three roots the last root's syllable carries the stress. Since roots are monosyllabic and inflection is mostly prefixal, a prefixed verb is stressed on its root = final syllable, but with pronominal enclitics/suffixes the stress stays on the root (non-final). The language is also tonal (4 tones, §2.3) — stress statement coexists with tone.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; author says stress is fully predictable ('siempre'). (Arellanes 2009 notes polysyllabic Spanish loans exist but gives no stress rule for them.)
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the morphological word (inflected word incl. affixes; compounds). Statement is impressionistic/structuralist (author's §2.0: 'siguiendo la escuela estructuralista'), by a native-speaker linguist; no acoustic correlates of stress given. Arellanes 2009/2010 independently confirm roots are monosyllabic bimoraic feet with affixes/clitics prosodically light, consistent with root stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All three opened sources describe the Zapotec of San Pablo Güilá (agencia of Santiago Matatlán, distrito de Tlacolula, Valle de Oaxaca) = Glottolog guil1236 / ISO ztu exactly; López Cruz is a native-speaker linguist from the community. No dialect mismatch.

sources.note: Ch.2 Fonología, §2.2 'Patrón acentual' (p.49): stress is predictable: in every inflected word stress falls on the root (radical); in compounds of 2-3 roots it falls on the syllable of the last root; no affix ever bears stress. §2.1 (p.47): roots predominantly monosyllabic; polysyllables arise from prefixes/suffixes or compounding. Tone (4 tones) treated separately in §2.3.

sources.note: No stress/accent section (a full-text search for stress/accent: 'acento' only in OT constraint glosses and a diachronic footnote). Ch.5 (pp.331-343): monomorphemic words are monosyllabic bimoraic feet (fortis codas moraic, lenis not); affixes, clitics and polysyllabic loans may have monomoraic syllables; fn.11 p.55: Proto-Zapotec unstressed (post-tonic) vowels were elided to reach monosyllabicity (*'do.pa > dop). Confirms root = the heavy syllable but gives no explicit placement rule.
